one_month_reasoning: I rechecked EDGAR on 10/2: there is no Q3 scheduling 8-K yet. Lattice reported Q3 2025 on Nov 3 and usually schedules about 12 days ahead, so Q3 2026 results most likely land Nov 3, after the window closes on Fri Oct 30. The in-window events are second-order. First, the first AMI lock-up tranche is about 1.19M shares (25% of the 4,741,352 common shares issued per the 7/27 8-K Item 3.02, corrected from my 1.3M); it frees on 10/25, a Sunday, so the shares are tradable from 10/26. That is about 0.8% of shares outstanding, and THL also holds block-trade rights. Second, the AMI financial-statements 8-K/A is due around mid-October. Third, hyperscaler and peer earnings arrive in late October. On the other side, pre-earnings positioning into a guide ($245-265M, EPS $0.54-0.58) already above stale estimates could lift the stock, while the +21% two-week run adds a little reversal risk. These roughly cancel, so I use a near-symmetric lognormal around $134 at 61%/3.5 = 17.4% monthly vol, shaded about 0.5 point down for the lock-up and block-trade overhang.

fair_value.method: P/E is NTM EPS at Oct 2027 of about $3.70 x 38 = $141. EV/sales is about $1.55B x 12, less about $0.5B net debt, over 146M diluted shares = $124. Weights 65/35 give about $135, essentially at the $134 spot.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct 2027 (Q4'27-Q3'28) of about $3.70 x 38 = $141. 2027E non-GAAP EPS of about $3.15 on about $1.35B revenue and 146M diluted shares.

inputs_detail.derivation: This is an oral statement on the Q2 call only. The press release states just '$1B+ run rate in Q3 2026'. I use it as an upper anchor, not as guidance.

My round-1 bottom-up was $1.38B (FPGA from the $220M Q3 midpoint at about 7% q/q, plus AMI above $200M x 1.25). I trim it toward the $1.33B S&P consensus because 'pretty much booked' is distributor backlog (distributors are 95% of revenue) and can be rescheduled.
The CFO's '70-ish%' gross margin. The Q3 opex guide of $83-90M includes 2 months of AMI; a full AMI quarter runs at about $95M, and I add modest growth.
$925M secured term loan at SOFR plus 1.00-1.75%, amortizing 1.25% per quarter, maturing 2031. The Q3 non-GAAP tax guide is 4-6%.
142.03M outstanding at 7/30 (includes 4,741,352 AMI shares), plus RSU and AMI employee-grant dilution. Corrected from 144M per the supervisor.

$1.35B x 70% - $400M = $545M, less $45M interest = $500M, less 6% tax = $470M, over 146M shares = $3.22. I shade it to $3.15, between my build and the supervisor's $3.06. Consensus is $3.21, so I add no edge over the Street on 2027.

2027E of $3.15 grown about 17-18%, lower than my round-1 20%. I no longer lean on the $3B-by-2030 figure, which the CEO called 'aspirational'. The input rests on the AMI +25% 2027 comment and FPGA attach growth.

Spot is about 42x consensus 2027 EPS of $3.21 (134/3.21), and about 36x my NTM at the horizon. I keep 38x, mild compression from today's NTM of about 44x, because growth is still 25%+ with a 40% FCF margin. I do not go higher, since consensus already sits at my 2027 number and there is no estimate-revision edge to pay up for.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Oct 2027 of about $1.55B x 12 = EV $18.6B, less net debt of about $0.5B, over 146M shares = $124.

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027E of $1.35B rolled forward at about 15% growth.

Current EV is about $19.8B (134 x 142M + about $0.8B net debt), about 15x NTM revenue. I compress to 12x for slowing growth and the firmware mix. I give this method lower weight because AMI's software mix makes it less comparable with FPGA peers.

About $0.8B at close ($925M drawn against roughly $100-130M of cash left). Combined FCF of about $100-130M a quarter is partly used for debt paydown toward the CFO's under-2x target, with buybacks likely resuming. Up from $0.45B in round 1.

bear.story: AI-server capex digests in 2027, or the distributor channel (95% of revenue; two distributors hold 88% of receivables) destocks as in 2024, when revenue fell about 30%. 2027 EPS comes in around $2.5-2.6, the multiple compresses to about 28-30x, and the about $0.8B of net debt amplifies the de-rating.

base.story: 2027 revenue lands near $1.33-1.35B (consensus), EPS about $3.15, NTM EPS about $3.7 at the horizon at about 38x. Net debt falls to about $0.5B and the AMI lock-up supply is absorbed.

bull.story: FPGA attach per AI server keeps rising and AMI grows 25%+. 2027 comes in well above consensus (about $1.5B) and the $3B 'aspirational' path starts to look real. NTM EPS of about $4.5 x about 46x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $87 (about 27-28x my 2027E EPS of about $3.15, and about 20% under the Aug-Sep lows of $104-111), the market would be pricing an end to the AI-server FPGA growth leg. Likely causes are a Q3/Q4 guide-down that shows the 'pretty much booked' 2027 was distributor stocking (95% distributor mix), an AI-server capex digestion, or AMI customer attrition. Ordinary 55-60% volatility would not usually take it there without such news.

reasoning: Round 2 keeps my primary-document build and applies the supervisor's fact checks. (1) Consensus 2027 EPS is $3.21 on $1.33B (S&P Global via StockAnalysis), not the stale $2.41 I cited. My own 2027E (round 1 $3.20) therefore adds no edge over the Street, so I no longer treat the stock as having upside from estimate revisions. (2) Diluted shares are about 146M, not 144M; the 142.03M at 7/30 already includes the 4,741,352 AMI shares. (3) The first lock-up tranche is about 1.19M shares, not 1.3M. (4) The $1.2B exit rate, '2027 pretty much booked' and '$3B by 2030' are call-only, and the CEO called the last one 'aspirational'. I trim 2027E revenue from $1.38B to $1.35B and NTM growth from 20% to about 17%, giving 2027E EPS of about $3.15 and NTM EPS of about $3.70 at the horizon. (5) Net debt at the horizon is about $0.5B, since buybacks may resume. Revalued, P/E is $141 (38x) and EV/sales is $124 (12x NTM, 146M shares). Weighted 65/35 they give $135, down from $138; the supervisor's $140 weights P/E about 0.8 and is in the same range. I agree with the supervisor that no search settles the multiple. I keep 38x rather than going higher because consensus already matches my numbers. Distribution: centred near spot with median about $134-135 and effective log-vol of about 0.55, below the 61% realized. Scenarios are 25/50/25 at $75/$140/$210, with the left tail kept fat because two distributors hold 88% of receivables and 95% of revenue goes through distributors. Net, the ladder moves down about 0.5-1 point in the middle versus round 1 (P(>=134) 0.505 versus 0.515), and the thesis break moves from $85 to $87 on the slightly lower EPS base. I rechecked EDGAR on 10/2: no new 8-K (no Q3 date, no AMI 8-K/A), only routine Forms 4 and 144. Research was limited to that one check plus the supervisor's verified facts.
